ai.literal: From whatever thing, from whatever thing, he who has renounced, suffering from that thing, from that thing, he does not have.
ai.translation: From whatever thing a person detaches themselves, from that very thing they are free from suffering.
ai.modern: ஒருவன் எந்தெந்தப் பொருள்களிலிருந்து விலகிப் பற்றற்றவனாக இருக்கிறானோ, அந்தந்தப் பொருள்களால் அவனுக்குத் துன்பம் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the direct relationship between renunciation and the cessation of suffering. The repetition of 'யாதனின்' (from whatever) and 'அதனின்' (from that) emphasizes that every single object or desire we let go of represents a specific source of pain that is eliminated. By systematically detaching ourselves from worldly things, we systematically insulate ourselves from the grief they inevitably bring. Thus, true freedom from sorrow is achieved not all at once, but progressively through gradual detachment.

ai.literal: If desiring to be attained, let one renounce; after renouncing, here, things that naturally belong are many.
ai.translation: If one desires the state of supreme joy to be attained, let them renounce. After renouncing, many are the joys that naturally follow in this very state.
ai.modern: ஒருவர் இன்பம் உண்டாக விரும்பினால் பற்றுகளைத் துறக்க வேண்டும்; அவ்வாறு துறந்த பிறகு, இவ்வுலகிலேயே அவருக்கு இயற்கையாகவே வந்து சேரும் நன்மைகள் பலவாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the immediate and spontaneous rewards of renunciation. If a person desires true, lasting happiness to arise, the path is to renounce worldly attachments. Once they have renounced, they do not experience a void; instead, many natural joys and benefits ('இயற்பால') spontaneously flow to them in this very life ('ஈண்டு'). The poet shows that true freedom brings an abundance of peace that cannot be acquired through possession.

ai.literal: Conquering is necessary of the five the sensory domain; renouncing is necessary desired things all together.
ai.translation: One must conquer the domain of the five senses, and simultaneously renounce all desired things of the world.
ai.modern: ஐந்து புலன்களின் வழியே செல்லும் ஆசையை வெல்ல வேண்டும்; விரும்பிய அனைத்தையும் ஒரே நேரத்தில் துறக்க வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the essential steps for true renunciation. The 'five' refers to the five senses, and 'pulam' represents their respective domains of desire. To succeed in asceticism, one must first conquer these sensory impulses. Along with this internal control, one must completely and simultaneously abandon all external attachments and desires. The poet emphasizes that both sensory mastery and the giving up of worldly desires must happen together for complete liberation.

ai.literal: The nature is for ascetic practice even one thing's absence; possession delusion becomes and further turning back.
ai.translation: The true nature of ascetic renunciation is to possess absolutely nothing; to possess even a single thing will lead one back into delusion.
ai.modern: ஒரு பொருளும் இல்லாமல் இருப்பதே தவத்தின் இயல்பான நிலையாகும்; ஏதேனும் ஒன்றை வைத்திருப்பது மீண்டும் மயக்கத்தை உண்டாக்கிப் பிறவிச் சுழற்சிக்குத் திருப்பிவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the absolute nature of renunciation. The natural state of true asceticism is the complete absence of any possession, even a single object. If an ascetic retains or desires even one possession, it acts as a seed of attachment, leading them back into the delusion of worldly life and rebirth. Thus, complete detachment is essential for spiritual liberation.

ai.literal: And further, attachment of what use indeed, for those who have undertaken the severing of birth, even the body is an excess.
ai.translation: For those who have resolved to sever the cycle of birth, even their own body is a superfluous burden; what use, then, are any other attachments?
ai.modern: பிறவிச் சுழற்சியை அறுக்க முயன்றவர்களுக்குத் தமது உடம்பே ஒரு சுமையாகும் போது, வேறு பிற பற்றுகள் எதற்காக?
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the absolute nature of renunciation. For those who have committed to ending the cycle of birth and death, even their own physical body is seen as an extra, unnecessary burden. If the very body they inhabit is considered superfluous to their spiritual goal, then any other worldly attachments are completely useless. The author uses this stark comparison to show that true renunciation requires letting go of all external bonds, as even the physical self is ultimately a temporary vessel to be transcended.

ai.literal: He who cuts off the delusion called 'I' and 'mine' will enter a world exalted even to the heavenly beings.
ai.translation: He who cuts off the delusion of 'I' and 'mine' will enter a realm that is higher than even the world of the heavenly beings.
ai.modern: "நான்", "எனது" என்கின்ற அகந்தையை ஒழிப்பவன், தேவர்களுக்கும் மேலான உயர்ந்த உலகத்தை அடைவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the ultimate reward of true renunciation. The poet identifies the root of all worldly attachment as the dual delusion of 'I' (egoism) and 'mine' (possessiveness), referred to here as 'cerukku' (delusion or pride). One who completely severs ('aṟuppāṉ') this deep-seated ignorance does not merely attain a temporary heaven. Instead, they enter a supreme state of liberation ('ulakam') that is far superior ('uyarnta') to the transient pleasures enjoyed even by the celestial beings ('vāṉōr').

ai.literal: Clinging, do not leave, sufferings, attachment, clinging, to those who do not let go.
ai.translation: Sufferings will cling to and never leave those who do not let go of their attachments.
ai.modern: பற்றுகளைப் பற்றிக்கொண்டு அவற்றை விடாதவர்களை, துன்பங்கள் பற்றிக்கொண்டு விடவே மாட்டா.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the inescapable cycle of desire and suffering. The poet uses the word 'பற்று' (grasp or attachment) in a dual sense: the mental grip we hold on worldly desires, and the grip that misery holds on us. Sufferings are personified as relentless forces that actively cling to and refuse to release those who refuse to let go of their own attachments. The only way to be freed from the grip of sorrow is to first release our own grasp on worldly things.

ai.literal: Those who attained the supreme state are those who renounced completely; being deluded, caught in the net are the other people.
ai.translation: Those who have completely renounced all attachments have attained the supreme state of liberation; all others, remaining deluded, are caught in the net of worldly bondage.
ai.modern: முற்றிலுமாகப் பற்றுகளைத் துறந்தவர்களே முக்தி நிலையை அடைந்தவர்கள் ஆவர்; அவ்வாறு துறக்காத மற்றவர்கள் மயக்கமுற்று உலக ஆசை என்னும் வலையில் சிக்கியவர்கள் ஆவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts those who achieve spiritual liberation with those who remain bound to worldly existence. The term 'தலைப்பட்டார்' refers to those who have reached the highest state of spiritual attainment, which is achieved only by those who have renounced everything completely ('தீரத் துறந்தார்'). On the other hand, those who do not renounce ('மற்றையவர்') remain in a state of delusion ('மயங்கி'). This delusion causes them to be trapped like prey in a net ('வலைப்பட்டார்'), representing the inescapable snare of worldly desires and attachments.

ai.literal: At the very moment attachment is severed, it severs rebirth; otherwise, impermanence will be experienced.
ai.translation: At the very moment attachment is severed, the cycle of rebirth is cut off; otherwise, one will only continue to experience the instability of existence.
ai.modern: பற்று நீங்கிய பொழுதே பிறவி அறுக்கப்படும்; இல்லையெனில், நிலையற்ற தன்மையே தொடர்ந்து காணப்படும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the immediate effect of renunciation on the cycle of rebirth. When all attachments are completely severed, the cause of rebirth is destroyed at that very instant. If one does not sever these attachments, they will continue to experience the painful, unstable cycle of impermanent worldly existence. The word 'kaṇṇē' emphasizes that liberation occurs simultaneously with the cessation of desire.

ai.literal: Clasp the attachment of Him who is without attachment; that attachment clasp, for attachments to be let go.
ai.translation: Clasp the attachment of Him who is free from all attachments; hold fast to that attachment so that you may let go of your own attachments.
ai.modern: பற்றுகள் இல்லாதவனுடைய பற்றினைப் பற்றிக் கொள்ளுங்கள்; நம்முடைய பற்றுகளை விடுவதற்காக அந்தப் பற்றினைப் பற்றிக் கொள்ளுங்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the path to complete renunciation through a beautiful play on the word 'patru', which means both 'attachment' and 'to hold fast'. The mind cannot remain entirely empty; to rid oneself of worldly desires, one must anchor the mind onto something that is completely free of attachments. By holding onto this pure, desireless attachment, one's own worldly bonds naturally fall away. Thus, the higher attachment becomes the tool to dissolve all lower attachments.
